summary: The Tipped Employee Protection Act modifies the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 by changing how a "tipped employee" is defined. It removes the requirement that an employee's specific job duties be considered when determining if they are a tipped employee, and instead bases the definition on whether the employee receives tips and cash wages equaling at least the federal minimum wage over a work period determined by the employer.

affected_groups.effect: Their status as tipped employees will be determined by their total tips and cash wages over an employer-determined work period, without regard to their specific job duties.
They gain the ability to determine the work period used for calculating whether a worker meets the definition of a tipped employee.

key_provisions: Excludes consideration of an employee's duties when determining if the worker is a tipped employee.
Expands the definition of a tipped employee to include any worker receiving tips and cash wages at a rate at least equal to the federal minimum wage.
Establishes that the work period used for this calculation is determined by the employer, such as a day, a week, two weeks, 28 days, or a pay period.
missing_information: The bill does not specify what happens if tips and cash wages fall below the federal minimum wage during an employer-determined work period.
The source material does not provide details on potential penalties for non-compliance.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Tipped Employee Protection Act modifies the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 by changing how a "tipped employee" is defined. It removes the requirement that an employee's specific job duties be considered when determining if they are a tipped employee, and instead bases the definition on whether the employee receives tips and cash wages equaling at least the federal minimum wage over a work period determined by the employer.
summary_detail.significance: This bill alters the standard definitions under federal labor law governing wage and hour rules for tipped workers by removing job-duties tests and allowing employers to set the calculation period.
